properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 7 at 3:47PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.Elevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at
Dunnellon due to excessive hydrilla growth along a 4.5 mile stretch
of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau. The hydrilla has been
acting like a dam and holding water back, keeping levels elevated.
With heavy rainfall occurring near Dunnellon, the river has continued
to rise and is forecast to remain in minor flood stage.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:45 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 28.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:45 PM EDT Wednesday was 28.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 28.6 feet
this evening.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.7
feet on 08/09/2003.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 400 AM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 7 at 12:11PM MST until October 8 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible. Afternoon temperatures
102 to 106. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...In Arizona, Gila River Valley and Parker Valley. In
California, Chuckwalla Valley and Palo Verde Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 AM MST /10 AM PDT/ to 8 PM MST /8 PM PDT/ Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible. Afternoon temperatures
103 to 107. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Yuma area.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 7 at 2:57PM EDT until October 7 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Western Manatee County in west central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 600 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 257 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Bradenton, Palmetto, Longboat Key, Anna Maria Island, Anna Maria,
West Bradenton, South Bradenton, West Samoset, Memphis, Ellenton,
Holmes Beach, Bradenton Beach, Palma Sola, Bayshore Gardens,
Samoset, Oneco and Cortez.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 7 at 12:55PM MDT until October 9 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Cheyenne WY
properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM FRIDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH FRIDAY
EVENING DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF NE AND
WY...

The National Weather Service in Cheyenne WY has issued a Fire Weather
Watch.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zones 417 through 422, 425, 427, 432,
and 434.

* TIMING...From Friday afternoon through Friday evening.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 12 to 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions are
possible during the valid watch time. These conditions could promote
the rapid spread of wildfires which could become life-threatening.

Follow all fire restrictions. Avoid activities that could cause
sparks.
